label: late copy phase, input d/w/m/y/h/k/l
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original inputs or the <DEL> step, and only on repeated inputs (in_first == 0). It is concentrated in the last three copy steps (to_go <= 2 holds 88% of the mass) and is strongest in short sequences (L = 3: 32% rate). Input token identity modulates it in a graded way: d is strongest (26% rate), then w, m, y, then h, k, l. The top activations are almost all d or w fed back at the last step of L = 3 sequences. Late copy steps alone give recall 0.84 but precision 0.18. Adding the token set raises precision to about 0.5 but drops mass recall to about 0.6, so the token dependence is soft and not a clean set. Rate falls with more digits in the sequence.
